problem.title: Triangle-Count Equidistribution and Local Limits
problem.statement: For fixed $p\in(0,1)$ and triangle count $X$ in $G(n,p)$, how far do asymptotic equidistribution of $X$ modulo $q$ and its local limit theorem extend beyond $q=o(n^2/\log n)$?
problem.background:
Collected from Oberwolfach Reports, which document mathematical workshops and their open-problem discussions.

**Source report:** [Combinatorics and Probability (2009), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2009/23, pp. 1225--1302](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2009/23)

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** partially solved

**Assessment.** The extension from triangle counts to fixed subgraph counts has substantial positive results: modular equidistribution is known in sparse regimes and local limit theorems are known for broad connected-subgraph regimes, but the full original analogue is not established.

**Sources checked.**

- [Oberwolfach Report 23, Combinatorics and Probability](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2009/23)
- [DeMarco-Kahn-Redlich modular subgraph statistics](https://doi.org/10.37236/4094)
- [Sah-Sawhney-Zhu joint local limit theorem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09535)

This is a dated literature triage derived from the supplied OWR curation; verify time-sensitive status and cited claims independently.
